Doppler DPU

This DPU implements the Doppler FFT (2D FFT).

Introduction

Description

This DPU expects as input the radar cube with 1D FFT data as described in DPIF_RADARCUBE_FORMAT_1. The output of this DPU is a detection matrix of format described in DPIF_DETMATRIX_FORMAT_1. These are the only formats supported by this DPU.

The Doppler DPU is available in HWA implementations:

DPU Implementation Runs on cores Uses HWA
dopplerProcHWA R5F or DSP Yes



DopplerProcHWA

Data from radar cube is moved into HWA memory using EDMA, HWA performs the required computations and data is moved by EDMA from HWA internal memory to the detection matrix.

The following figure shows a high level block diagram of the DPU implementation.

HWA based Doppler DPU High Level block diagram

A list of resources required by this DPU is described in DPU_DopplerProcHWA_HW_Resources_t. In particular, the number of EDMA channels required is constant and does not depend on the DPU configuration. On the other hand, the number of required HWA paramsets is a function of the number of TX antennas configured in the data path as described in DPU_DopplerProcHWA_HwaCfg_t.

Besides the resources described above, other parameters required for the DPU configuration are listed in DPU_DopplerProcHWA_StaticConfig_t. In particular, the DPU takes as input the number of Doppler chirps (numDopplerChirps), which does not need to be a power of two. It produces a detection matrix of Doppler dimension equal to numDopplerBins which must be a power of 2 greater or equal than numDopplerChirps. Another DPU input is the number of range bins, which must be even but does not need to be a power of two.

This DPU supports static clutter removal feature. This feature is enabled/disabled via dynamic configuration listed in DPU_DopplerProc_StaticClutterRemovalCfg_t. When static clutter removal is enabled, the mean value of the input samples to the Doppler FFT is subtracted from the samples.

Parameter Restriction
numDopplerChirps None.
numDopplerBins Must be power of two greater or equal than numDopplerChirps.
numRangeBins Must be even.

Below are details of the DPU implementation:
EDMA is used to move data from the radar cube into the HWA internal memory and after processing is done to move data from HWA internal memory to the detection matrix. All 8 HWA memory banks are required by this DPU, regardless of the DPU configuration. In this document, the HWA memory banks are called M0, M1, ..., M7. Each memory bank has a size of 16KB.
A ping/pong buffer scheme is used where:
The two pairs of contagious memory banks (M0,M1) and (M4,M5) are used for ping input/output processing, and the other two pairs (M2,M3) and (M6,M7) are used for pong input/output processing. In this document, the pairs of contagious memory banks are called MP0 (M0,M1), MP1 (M2,M3), MP2 (M4,M5) and MP3 (M5,M7).

In each iteration (ping/pong), a column of the radar cube matrix is brought into HWA for processing. Such column consists of all samples for a fixed range, that is, all received virtual antennas for all Doppler chirps for a fixed range bin.
The steps below are executed by HWA on data (one column of the radar cube as described above) sitting in its M memory. The description below is given for processing the ping buffer. Pong buffer processing is identical to ping, except that MP0 is replaced by MP1 and MP2 is replaced by MP3.

Windowing
Before FFT operation, input samples are multiplied by a window function. Window size and coefficients are defined in DPU_DopplerProcHWA_HwaCfg_t. Window coefficients must be provided by application.

FFT and Log2|.|
In this step 2D FFT and Log2 of the absolute value of each sample is computed. Input samples are in MP0 and output samples are in MP2. Input sample is of type cmplx16ImRe_t and output is of type uint16_t. This step also converts the number of input samples from N = numDopplerChirps to a number of output samples K = numDopplerBins, which is the size of the Doppler FFT. Both numDopplerBins and numDopplerChirps are input parameters for this DPU and numDopplerBins must be a power of 2 greater or equal than numDopplerChirps.

Summation
Summation of all virtual antennas is computed for each Doppler bin.
The output of the previous step (HWA Log2 magnitude) is in Q11 format. The sum is done using FFT in HWA, the sum is obtained in the DC (0th) bin. Input of the summation is on MP2 and output is on MP0. This FFT programming has srcScale of 3, meaning 3 redundant bits (sign extension, in this case unsigned) are added to MSB and 5 LSBs are padded with 0, so input before computation is in Q[11 + 5] format. The dstScale is set to 8, so summation output will have 8-bits dropped, giving a result in Q[11 + 5 - 8] = Q8 format. The FFT size is the next power of 2 of number of virtual antennas and the FFT is programmed to enable all butterfly scaling stages, hence the FFT output will be 1/N' * sum(.), where N' = 2^Ceil(Log2(N)), where N = numVirtualAntennas. The sum output which is input to CFAR is in Q8 format, so the CFAR threshold-scale also needs to be in Q8 format. If CFAR threshold is originally intended to be expressed in dB (say for user friendliness), then we need to do some translation before feeding to the CFAR algorithm. This can be derived as follows:
Let N be the number of virtual antennas and N' = 2^ceil(log2(N)) and user friendly CFAR threshold in dB is TdB (= 20*log10(|.|)). CFAR needs to do in general:
CUT (Cell Under Test) = 1/N * sum(log10(|.|)) > TdB/20 + average of noise terms [similar looking to CUT on LHS]
Given log10(|.|) = log2(|.|)/log2(10), and further adjusting the terms to do computation similar to match what is the sum output described above :
2^8 * 1/ N' * sum(log2(|.|)) > TdB/20*log2(10)*2^8 * (N/N') + average of noise terms [similar looking to CUT on LHS]
So the CFAR threshold to be provided to the CFAR algorithm operating on this doppler DPU output is
T = 256 * TdB / 6 * N / N'

Once the summation is computed for all Doppler bins, EDMA transfers the result from MP0 to the detection matrix.

HWA memory bank size limitation
The following 2 conditions must be satisfied for the parameters in this DPU configuration:
4 x numRxAntennas x numTxAntennas x numDopplerChirps <= 32768
2 x numRxAntennas x numTxAntennas x numDopplerBins <= 32768

The reason for this limitation is as follows:
The size of the data that is brought in for processing in HWA (per ping/pong iteration) is a column of the radar cube. The size of radar cube column is
4 x numRxAntennas x numTxAntennas x numDopplerChirps (I),
where 4 bytes is sizeof(cmplx16ImRe_t), the sample size.
After the 2D FFT and Log2|.| , we go from Doppler chirps to Doppler bins and from cmplx16ImRe_t to uint16_t.
Therefore the size after 2D FFT and Log2|.| is
2 x numRxAntennas x numTxAntennas x numDopplerBins (II),
where 2 bytes is sizeof(uint16_t).

Both quantities above (I and II) should fit (independently) in one of the HWA memory pairs which has a size of 32KB.

Exported APIs
DPU initialization is done through DPU_DopplerProcHWA_init.

DPU configuration is done by DPU_DopplerProcHWA_config. The configuration can only be done after the DPU has been initialized. The configuration parameters are described in DPU_DopplerProcHWA_Config.

The DPU is executed by calling DPU_DopplerProcHWA_process.
This will trigger the first ping/pong EDMA transfers and from there on, the processing of the Doppler DPU for the full radar cube is driven by hardware: EDMA will move data in and trigger HWA, which will process the data and trigger EDMA to move data out (to detection matrix) and trigger next EDMA to move data in – and so on. All columns of the radar cube matrix will be processed in this loop and no CPU intervention is needed. When HWA finishes processing all columns of the radar cube it will generate an interrupt. When the last EDMA transfer to the detection matrix has landed, EDMA will generate an interrupt. The DPU processing is done when both interrupts are received. Static Clutter Removal
Static clutter removal is performed entirely in HWA. When enabled, the mean value of the input samples to the Doppler FFT is subtracted from the samples. The samples with subtracted mean value are then multiplied by Doppler FFT window and then fed to the FFT engine. The following two figures shows data path with the static clutter removal feature (enabled and disabled). The same ping/pong buffer scheme is used, except that the static clutter removal is inserted before Doppler FFT. It is performed using two param sets per tx antenna. The first param set (labeled as "DC Est" in figure below) performs DC estimation for each Rx antenna on the data located in MP0. The estimation scaling parameters are computed by DPU_DopplerProcHWA_calcDCEstimParams and stored in the common HWA registers during the configuration time. The second param set (labeld as "DC sub") performs DC subtraction, and transfers data to MP2 and at the same time transposes the first and the second index, (tx antenna index and chirp index), so that the following Doppler FFT is computed using one param set on all virtual antennas of the current range bin. The FFT data are copied back to MP0. The final summation param takes data from MP0 and copies the result to MP2 again, from where it is transferred out using EDMA to detection matrix in L3 memory.

Note that because of the limitation of the DC estimation scale parameters, which could be programmed only for the number of samples (chirps) more than 32, when the number of chirps is less or equal to 32, an extra gain is applied in DC estimate stage in the input formatter, using a scale shift. This extra gain is removed in the DC subtraction stage. In addition, clutter removal could have been done in two stages, with DC subtraction being part of the Doppler FFT param set, but since its input data are already feed with the maximum gain (input formatter scale = 0), and we wanted to maintain the same gain down the data path, including visualizer, we implemented the three stage approach at the expense of additional latency.
